messages:
olivia-support: Heads up — Acme reports that two org admins hit 403 on the console after we ran the staged SSO proxy exchange last night. They could view the org earlier this morning; after the swap they can see the org but all actions are blocked.
kevin-eng: Oof. Any error details or request IDs from their attempts?
olivia-support: Customer pasted a screenshot, says error shows "403 permission denied: missing org.admin role". They included a request id: req_0a7f3c. I asked for HAR and headers, waiting.
acme-note (copied by olivia-support): "We were able to click into Org -> Members but all admin buttons are grayed and API returns 403 for admin endpoints."
nina-sre: Can you repro with our staging SSO proxy? If it's a token claim/audience issue we should see it in the auth logs. I pulled proxy logs around the exchange: 
```
2026-03-12T02:13:05Z proxy[exchange]: session-token-exchange success user=joe@acme.com sub=U123 aud=console-service
2026-03-12T02:13:06Z proxy[exchange]: session-token-exchange success user=sara@acme.com sub=U124 aud=internal-idp
2026-03-12T02:13:06Z auth-service: token-audit WARN token_aud_mismatch sub=U124 expected=console-service got=internal-idp req=req_0a7f3c
```
nina-sre: That second line stands out — one user got aud=internal-idp. If the audience doesn't match our expected resource, our RBAC layer rejects admin claims.
okta-sync-bot: SCIM sync completed for acme-okta at 2026-03-12T02:00:00Z; no group membership changes detected.
kevin-eng: Good catch. Does the token from the proxy still contain org claims (e.g., roles or groups)? If proxy swapped to an internal audience, maybe it also stripped custom claims. Ask customer for a bearer token header (or a redacted JWT) so we can inspect payload.
olivia-support: Customer sent back a redacted JWT. I pasted it below with only payload: 
```
{"sub":"U124","email":"sara@acme.com","roles":[],"aud":"internal-idp","org_id":"acme-corp"}
```
olivia-support: Notice roles is empty. Before the swap it used to be ["org.admin","project.owner"].
sam-devex: That explains 403. Our RBAC checks for roles claim and for audience==console-service. Two separate failures: (1) proxy replaced/normalized claims to internal audience, (2) proxy dropped custom "roles" claim. Both can cause admin actions to be denied.
kevin-eng: Repro steps to validate in staging: 
1) Use staged proxy exchange flow (dev/test) against acme test org.
2) Get session token via proxy: 
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://staging-console.redwood.com/api/v1/orgs/acme-corp/members
```
3) Inspect JWT payload: `jwt decode $TOKEN` and check `aud` and `roles`.
kevin-eng: If aud != console-service or roles missing, you'll see failing Admin endpoints return 403 with error code AUTHZ_MISS_ROLE.
oncall: Is there a short mitigation we can give Acme? They are blocked on a release.
olivia-support: I proposed two workarounds to them: (A) we can invite an alternate admin (invite link) if they have another admin user not affected, or (B) we can temporarily promote a support-managed service account via internal admin API (manual fix) — requires SRE approval and logs.
kevin-eng: For (B) I can run a one-off script to patch their org membership claims server-side to restore org.admin for sara@acme.com. Command (internal only): 
```
POST https://internal-admin.redwood/api/orgs/acme-corp/members/patch
{ "email": "sara@acme.com", "add_roles": ["org.admin"] }
```
kevin-eng: But that's a bandaid. Root cause: our staged SSO proxy exchange config inadvertently used the upstream idp audience and dropped vendor-specific claims during token reissuance. We need a fix: ensure proxy preserves the roles claim or maps group->roles and sets aud to console-service.
kevin-eng: I opened infra ticket INFRA-1229 to patch the exchange mapping and added tests for claim passthrough. ETA for deploy: 24-48h if no regressions.
sam-devex: Short-term config change: set proxy flag passthrough_custom_claims=true for the acct to avoid claim scrub on the next rotation. That's low-risk and reversible. Recommend we toggle for Acme immediately.
oncall: Approve?
nina-sre: Approved for Acme only. I'll coordinate the change and roll back if we see errors.
olivia-support: I'll tell customer we can do a temporary server-side role patch now or flip passthrough_custom_claims for their tenant and monitor. Which do you prefer?
kevin-eng: Flip passthrough first, monitor auth logs for tokens containing roles and aud=console-service, then reconcile memberships. If still failing, run the patch.
olivia-support: Noted. I'll update ticket and post follow-ups here. Customer impact: two org admins across two teams affected, started ~02:12Z.
kevin-eng: Post-mortem action items: 1) fix INFRA-1229 mapping, 2) add integration test for SSO proxy exchanges preserving roles, 3) add alert when token aud mismatches expected resource to catch before customer-facing failures.
olivia-support: Thanks team — I'll message Acme with the temporary plan (enable passthrough flag, monitor, then reconcile). Will update thread after change. :thumbsup:
